code_paper_alignment.methodology_matches.reason: The integrand-circuit decoherence implementation materially differs from the reported ASAP layer schedule. It applies gates in input order and flushes relaxation only when a new maximum layer is encountered, permitting gates assigned to earlier layers to execute after their relaxation. This is not equivalent to scheduled channel execution. Resource bookkeeping on the saved U=10 trivial ansatz gives 78.69 ms of streaming relaxation versus 86.67 ms under the stated ASAP rule, excluding preparation and measurement overhead.
evidence: proposal/report.tex:260-265 states that all qubits undergo relaxation for every ASAP-scheduled layer, with duration determined by whether that layer contains a CNOT.
proposal/code/noisesim.py:236-246 implements that schedule for Hadamard circuits.
proposal/code/noisy_eval.py:113-141 instead processes prefix gates immediately and flushes only when lay > cur_layer; gates with lay < cur_layer are still applied immediately.
proposal/logs/trajectory_U10_trivial.npz: ops_x/ops_z contain the 145 operators used for the duration calculation; compile.py:109-127 defines the stated ASAP schedule.
proposal/code/noisy_eval.py:147-150 and 166-171 also assign a single relaxation duration to measurement basis changes, including two-gate Y-basis rotations.
